steps.title: Grow Solanum okadae seedlings
steps.instruction: Obtain seeds of Solanum okadae (accession OKA 7129) from the James Hutton Institute, germinate and grow them in a glasshouse at 22 °C ± 2 °C with a 16 h photoperiod until plants are 2 weeks old; use young leaves for downstream work.

steps.title: Prepare 1× TBE buffer
steps.instruction: Mix 100 mL of 10× UltraPure™ TBE buffer (Invitrogen, cat 15581‑044) with 900 mL distilled water to obtain 1 L of 1× TBE; store at room temperature.

steps.title: Make 0.8 % agarose gel with EtBr
steps.instruction: Dissolve 0.8 g agarose (Sigma‑Aldrich, cat A9539‑500G) in 100 mL 1× TBE buffer, heat until fully melted, cool for 5 min, add 5 µL ethidium bromide (Fisher Bioreagents, cat BP1302‑10) just before pouring into a casting tray; allow the gel to set.

steps.title: Extract genomic DNA
steps.instruction: Grind ~500 mg of fresh leaf tissue in liquid nitrogen with a mortar and pestle, weigh 100 mg of the resulting powder, transfer to a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube and keep on ice (or freeze at –70 °C); extract DNA using the GenElute™ Plant Genomic DNA Miniprep kit (Sigma‑Aldrich, cat G2N70‑1KT) according to the manufacturer’s protocol; quantify DNA with a NanoDrop spectrophotometer, expecting an A260/A280 ratio of ~1.8 (a ratio of 2.0 indicates RNA contamination); store DNA for 1–4 weeks at 2–8 °C for short‑term use or 1–2 years at –20 °C for long‑term storage, avoiding repeated freeze‑thaw cycles.

steps.title: Design degenerate primers
steps.instruction: Retrieve the amino‑acid sequence of a known S‑locus F‑box protein (e.g., Petunia integrifolia subsp. inflata SLF, accession AAS79485) from NCBI or UniProt; run a protein‑protein BLAST against the nr database limited to Solanum (taxid 4107); filter hits to 60‑80 % identity and open the Multiple Alignment view; select a conserved region 150‑500 bp long and place forward and reverse primers in the most conserved stretches; design primers containing 5‑7 amino acids (~15‑20 bp); translate the chosen peptide to nucleotides with EMBOSS Backtranseq using the Solanum tuberosum codon‑usage table; replace variable positions with IUPAC ambiguity codes (Table 1) to generate degenerate primers (see Table 2); note that forward and reverse primers may differ in melting temperature by up to 6 °C, which is acceptable.

steps.title: Set up degenerate PCR
steps.instruction: In a clean PCR tube, assemble a 20 µL reaction containing 10‑50 ng template DNA, 4 µL MyTaq 5× reaction buffer (Bioline, cat BIO‑21126), 1 µL forward primer (10 µM), 1 µL reverse primer (10 µM), 0.5 µL MyTaq DNA polymerase (5 U/µL), and nuclease‑free water to 20 µL; include a water‑only negative control.

steps.title: Run PCR thermal program
steps.instruction: Place the tubes in a thermal cycler with the lid pre‑heated to 105 °C and run the following program: initial denaturation 94 °C for 2 min; 35 cycles of 94 °C for 30 s denaturation, annealing at the primer‑specific temperature (50‑65 °C) for 30 s, extension at 72 °C for 1 min; final extension at 72 °C for 10 min; hold at 4 °C indefinitely.

steps.title: Electrophorese PCR products
steps.instruction: Prepare a fresh 0.8 % agarose gel with EtBr as in step 3, immerse it in 1× TBE running buffer, mix 10‑12 µL of each PCR reaction with 0.5‑2.0 µL 5× blue loading buffer to achieve a 5× final concentration, load the wells alongside a 1 kb DNA HyperLadder (Bioline, cat BIO‑33053), and run at 65‑100 V for 60‑75 min.

steps.title: Visualize and excise DNA bands
steps.instruction: Using a UV transilluminator (wear appropriate UV protection), locate the band of the expected size, cut the gel slice as close to the DNA as possible with a clean scalpel and forceps, weigh the slice in a pre‑weighed 1.5 mL tube and record the weight.

steps.title: Purify DNA from gel
steps.instruction: Purify the excised fragment with the GeneJET Gel Extraction kit (Thermo Scientific, cat K0691) according to the manufacturer’s instructions.

steps.title: Sequence PCR amplicons
steps.instruction: Submit purified PCR products <800 bp for Sanger sequencing via the SpeedREAD service (SourceBioscience) using the same primers employed for amplification; for amplicons >800 bp, first clean the product with a PCR‑cleanup column or repeat gel extraction to remove excess primers and dNTPs before sequencing.
